admission.contract: A client-supplied FLAC stream is admitted into the issue-relevant bitreader path when `FLAC__stream_decoder_process_single` reaches partitioned-Rice residual decoding and calls `FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block` for at least one sample.
admission.predicate: process.hit && rice_call.hit && rice_call.time >= process.time && rice_call.nvals > 0 && rice_call.parameter < 32 && rice_call.input != 0
limitations: This binds admission to the `process_single` API path; the library also exposes other decode entrypoints.
It shows accepted traversal into Rice residual decoding, not the exact external byte sequence that caused it.

root.contract: During Rice block decoding, the scalar fallback leaves the bitreader fully exhausted at its buffer capacity, with no partial tail word and more residual values still pending.
root.predicate: fallback_state.hit && fallback_state.consumed_words == fallback_state.words && fallback_state.words == fallback_state.capacity && fallback_state.bytes == 0 && fallback_state.remaining > 0
limitations: The source shows this exhausted state is dangerous, but the public issue does not identify the exact malformed frame layout that produces it.
If `words < capacity`, the same state would not by itself prove an out-of-bounds access.

target.contract: The same exhausted full-buffer state is consumed by the subsequent read of `br->buffer[cwords]` in `FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block`.
target.predicate: buffer_read.hit && root.fallback_state.hit && buffer_read.time >= root.fallback_state.time && buffer_read.cwords == root.fallback_state.consumed_words && buffer_read.words == root.fallback_state.words && buffer_read.words == buffer_read.capacity && buffer_read.bytes == 0 && buffer_read.remaining > 0
limitations: This binds the dangerous operation to the root state from source inspection only; no runtime trace is available here.
The contract identifies the array read site, but actual fault manifestation depends on allocator/layout details outside the issue text and source alone.
